ctsem

Source: R/ctsem-package.R
ctsem-package.Rd

ctsem fits continuous and discrete time dynamic models to longitudinal data: panel data, intensive longitudinal data or a single time series, with observations at any times. The processes can interact, be of higher order or nonlinear, and be measured by continuous, binary, ordinal, count or censored variables. Any parameter can differ between subjects, at one or more levels, and depend on covariates. Estimation is by maximum likelihood, or Bayesian by optimisation or sampling, with an engine written in Julia (the default) or with Stan.

Details

A model is specified with ctModel, or in lavaan, Mplus or formula syntax with ctModelLavaan, ctModelMplus and ctModelFormula, and fitted with ctFit. summary(), ctDiscretePars, ctPredict and ctSubjectPars describe a fit, and ctScoreTest, ctFitAdequacy and ctModelImprove check and improve it. ctJuliaInstall sets up the Julia engine.

vignette('ctsem') works through a first analysis, and the website, https://cdriveraus.github.io/ctsem/, has the vignettes and the help pages grouped by task. For the original OpenMx based ctsem, see the ctsemOMX package. citation('ctsem') gives the references to cite.

References

Driver, C. C., Oud, J. H. L., & Voelkle, M. C. (2017). Continuous time structural equation modeling with R package ctsem. Journal of Statistical Software, 77(5), 1-35. doi:10.18637/jss.v077.i05

Driver, C. C., & Voelkle, M. C. (2018). Hierarchical Bayesian continuous time dynamic modeling. Psychological Methods, 23(4), 774-799. doi:10.1037/met0000168
